title: Hurricane Erin 2025 weakens but powerful storm 'could double or even triple in size': What we know so far | Today News
content: Hurricane Erin, the first hurricane of the 2025 Atlantic season, has weakened to a Category 3 hurricane but is expected to double or even triple in size as it moves north and west. Forecasters warn of a growing risk of life-threatening surf and rip currents along the US Eastern seaboard. The storm is not expected to directly hit the US East Coast, but its impacts threaten the North Carolina Outer Banks. As per CNN, Erin went from a Category 1 hurricane with 75 mph winds to a Category 5 with near 160 mph winds in just over 24 hours, making it one of the fastest-strengthening Atlantic hurricanes on record. Richard Pasch of the National Hurricane Center said, 'You're dealing with a major hurricane. The intensity is fluctuating. It's a dangerous hurricane in any event.' The storm's rapid intensification has been linked to climate change, which is causing the atmosphere to hold more water vapor and spiking ocean temperatures. Heavy rain and strong winds are expected across the Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico, with rainfall of 3 to 6 inches and 8 inches in some isolated areas. 'You're dealing with a major hurricane. The intensity is fluctuating. It's a dangerous hurricane in any event,' said Richard Pasch of the National Hurricane Center.

title: Hurricane Erin tracker: Latest path for first hurricane of Atlantic season
content: Hurricane Erin, the first hurricane of the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, is currently a Category 1 storm with maximum sustained winds up to 75 mph. According to forecasters, Erin is expected to pass near or north of the Leeward Islands on Saturday and could bring up to 6 inches of rain. The storm is forecast to become a Category 3 hurricane on Sunday with winds up to 125 mph and could grow further into a Category 4 on Monday with gusts reaching 140 mph. The National Hurricane Center predicted an above-normal hurricane season for the Atlantic, with August, September, and October being the most active months. Despite the threat of strong waves along the East Coast, a cold front is expected to keep Erin out to sea and bring below-average temperatures to the Northeast next week.

title: Hurricane Erin's Fierce Rumble: Unleashing Nature's Wrath | Science-Environment
content: Hurricane Erin, the first hurricane of the 2025 Atlantic season, has downgraded from Category 5 to Category 4. The storm is moving west-northwest at 14 mph, threatening heavy rainfall and swells across the northern Leeward Islands and Puerto Rico. Meteorologists warn of possible wildfire risks if conditions align unfavorably. According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center, Erin's maximum sustained winds have decreased to 140 mph from 160 mph. The Bahamas has issued a Tropical Storm Watch for the southeastern territories, while insurance experts project the storm will remain far offshore, sparing the U.S. East Coast from serious impacts.

title: Stronger, bigger Hurricane Erin forecast to create dangerous surf along US coast - WSVN 7News | Miami News, Weather, Sports | Fort Lauderdale
content: Hurricane Erin has reintensified to a Category 4 storm with 130 mph maximum sustained winds and is forecast to create dangerous surf and rip currents along the U.S. East Coast this week. The storm is moving northwest at 13 mph and is expected to remain a large, major hurricane into midweek. The area of strong winds is expected to grow more over the next few days, impacting coastal areas even though it isn't forecast to make a direct landfall. Richard Pasch of the National Hurricane Center said, 'You're dealing with a major hurricane. The intensity is fluctuating. It's a dangerous hurricane in any event.' The storm has already caused power outages and flight cancellations in Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands, and life-threatening surf and rip currents are forecast for the Bahamas, Bermuda, the U.S. East Coast, and Canada's Atlantic coast as Erin turns north and then northeast. Scientists have linked the rapid intensification of hurricanes in the Atlantic to climate change, which is causing the atmosphere to hold more water vapor and spiking ocean temperatures.

title: Stronger, bigger Hurricane Erin forecast to create dangerous surf along US coast - The Boston Globe
content: Hurricane Erin, a major hurricane, is forecast to create dangerous surf along the US coast. As of 2 a.m. Monday, Erin was located 110 miles northeast of Grand Turk Island and 935 miles south-southeast of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina. The storm is expected to remain large and powerful into midweek, with hurricane-force winds extending up to 60 miles from the center and tropical-storm-force winds extending up to 230 miles. According to Richard Pasch of the National Hurricane Center, 'You're dealing with a major hurricane. The intensity is fluctuating. It's a dangerous hurricane in any event.' The storm's outer bands have already caused power outages and flight cancellations in Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands. Life-threatening surf and rip currents are forecast for the Bahamas, Bermuda, the US East Coast, and Canada's Atlantic coast as Erin turns north and then northeast.

title: Hurricane Erin Downgraded to Category 3, Raising New Concerns | Science-Environment
content: Hurricane Erin, the first named storm of the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, has been downgraded from Category 5 to Category 3. The storm is expected to graze the Turks and Caicos and Bahamas, causing dangerous waves. Forecasters warn that swells from Erin will impact a vast range from the Bahamas to Atlantic Canada, posing life-threatening risks from surf and rip currents. Additionally, concerns about wildfire risks are rising if wind and dry conditions persist with the storm offshore. According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center, Erin's sustained winds have eased from 160 mph to 125 mph, and the storm is expected to turn north by early next week.

title: Category 4 Hurricane Erin moves past northern Caribbean islands, not forecast to hit land - Conservative Angle
content: Hurricane Erin, the first Atlantic hurricane of 2025, rapidly intensified from a tropical storm to a Category 5 storm in a single day, with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph). Although the storm's center is not expected to strike land, it threatens to dump flooding rains on islands in the region. Mike Brennen, director of the National Hurricane Center, said Erin grew into a 'very powerful hurricane,' with its winds gaining 60 mph (96 kph) in about nine hours. The storm is expected to remain a major hurricane until late next week, with powerful rip currents potentially affecting the U.S. East Coast from Florida to the mid-Atlantic. Scientists have linked rapid intensification of hurricanes in the Atlantic to climate change, with warmer ocean temperatures and increased water vapor in the atmosphere contributing to the storms' strengthening. Erin is the fifth named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season, which is expected to be unusually busy, with six to 10 hurricanes predicted, including three to five reaching major status.
